decisive_items: a well-defined T1-hypointense, STIR-hyperintense lesion with a thick sclerotic rim in the anterolateral cortex of the left femoral head
mild to moderate chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates
response.rationale: Sterile chronic bone lesion with a thick sclerotic rim, adjacent synovitis, normal inflammatory markers, and failure of anti-tubercular therapy favor chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis/CRMO over neoplastic or synovial-proliferative mimics.

rejected.why: No intra-articular loose bodies or chondroid bodies are described; the cortical bone lesion and sterile lymphoplasmacytic synovitis are not characteristic of synovial osteochondromatosis.
LCH would typically show Langerhans cells on biopsy and more lytic/punched-out bone lesions, not a thick sclerotic rim with lymphoplasmacytic synovitis.
Synovial sarcoma is a soft-tissue neoplasm; the biopsy lacks malignant spindle cells and the imaging shows an intraosseous sclerotic lesion rather than a joint-based soft-tissue mass.
